system.name: ASDR
system.one_liner: an algorithm-architecture co-design that accelerates neural rendering (NeRF) on computing-in-memory hardware via adaptive sampling and data reuse

components.name: Embedding Tables
components.role: original per-resolution feature tables (e.g. 16^3, 20^3, 25^3, 32^3 items) before hashing

components.name: HTs (Length=2^19)
components.role: fixed-length hash tables produced from the embedding tables; storing only one copy limits storage utilization and parallel access

components.name: Copied Tables
components.role: low-resolution tables stored without hashing and replicated into multiple copies for higher storage utilization and parallel access

content.key_idea: Hashing embedding tables into a single fixed-length hash table wastes storage and limits parallel access; ASDR instead stores unhashed low-resolution tables in multiple replicated copies to raise both storage utilization and parallel access.
content.reading_order: Panel (a) on the left shows several Embedding Tables of different sizes hashed into HTs; panel (b) shows sampled points from multiple rays landing in a shared 3D voxel grid; the right side compares HTs (sad face, low utilization) against Copied Tables (happy face, high utilization).

palette.used_for: stored-item cell fill in the hash-table boxes

style.stroke: thin black borders, square corners on table cells
style.arrows: thin solid arrow for the Hash operation
style.icons: sad-face and happy-face icons in the right-hand comparison boxes; camera icon in panel (b)

encoding.color_means: yellow-filled cells mark points-in-voxel / stored items, gray cells mark unused or other-point storage
encoding.emphasis: side-by-side sad-face vs. happy-face comparison boxes explicitly rank the single-copy hash table against the proposed copied-table scheme on storage utilization and parallel access

evidence: several consecutive sample points on a ray can be indexed in the low-resolution space using the embedded features of eight vertices
we utilize the observed storage headroom by adopting a de-hashed indexing approach for low-resolution tables and replicating multiple copies

summary: This figure motivates ASDR's de-hashed, replicated storage scheme for low-resolution embedding tables. Panel (a), 'Hash Mapping for Low Resolution Tables', shows several Embedding Tables of different sizes (e.g. 16^3, 20^3, 25^3, 32^3 items) each hashed into a fixed-length hash table, HTs (Length=2^19). Panel (b), 'Sampled points from multiple rays', shows a camera casting multiple rays into a shared 3D voxel grid, illustrating that many sampled points land in the same voxels. The right side directly compares the two storage strategies with sad/happy-face icons: the single-copy HTs box is marked with a sad face for low storage utilization and limited parallel access, while the Copied Tables box (128 copies of a 16^3-item table) is marked with a happy face for high storage utilization and highly parallel access.
summary_zh: 该图对比两种嵌入表存储方案：单份哈希表（HTs）因存储利用率低、并行访问受限被标为差评；ASDR 提出的多副本存储表（Copied Tables）通过复制未哈希的低分辨率表实现高利用率与高并行访问，被标为好评。
notes: The body paragraph discusses Figure 11(b) sampled points directly but attributes the de-hashing/address-generation mechanics mainly to Figures 12 and 14; those later-figure details were not attributed to Fig. 11 in this record.
